provenance.method: Safety boundary route separating dysphagia from sensory eating and ARFID.

question: Eating is difficult because I cough, choke or feel food sticking. Is that the same as sensory eating or ARFID?
why_it_matters: Swallowing problems can carry choking, dehydration and chest-infection risks and should not be misclassified as preference or executive-function difficulty.
current_understanding: No. Coughing or choking while eating/drinking, food feeling stuck, a wet/gurgly voice or similar symptoms can indicate a swallowing problem and need appropriate clinical assessment. Dysphagia, ARFID and sensory food preference are different categories even though they can coexist.
evidence_needed: Equivalent nation-specific swallowing-service navigation where it changes the practical route.
reopening_conditions: National urgent-care guidance or specialist referral responsibilities change materially.
dissent: Some eating difficulty has multiple interacting causes; separation of categories should not prevent multidisciplinary assessment.
